title: Four selected CHIME repeaters show no clear daily peak-frequency persistence in Catalog 2
abstract: We test daily spectral persistence in four repeating fast radio burst sources with at least 20 accepted days in CHIME/FRB Catalog 2 release 20251231. Successive detected days with gaps at most 30 days show no clear reduction in squared peak-frequency changes against random day order. Source probabilities range from 0.334 to 0.812. Quality cuts and a local 90-day shuffle retain the null result. A positive lag coefficient fitted on early days gives no useful prediction gain on later days. Three coefficients equal zero; the fourth slightly increases later error. Artificial ordering tests show useful sensitivity to strong daily-index persistence, with weaker power in small samples. The result applies to selected detections and fitted first-component peaks. It gives no physical memory-time limit, instrument correction, or independent telescope confirmation. The package includes code, aggregate results, a figure, exact source hashes, and external retrieval steps. Raw data and record-level extracts are excluded because their redistribution terms are not clear. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-6bd3e7eb032c; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.

display.caption: The full-record daily difference tests show no clear excess similarity. Early positive lag fits give no later prediction gain. Intervals condition on the early fit and resample blocks of later forecast edges. Zero intervals follow from zero fitted lag coefficients.
